utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Case Number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Stefan Waespi and Daryl Mundis, assisted by our manager, Andres Vatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have appearances for Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, lead counsel, and Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Second Defence team. Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and our legal assistant, Nermin Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today on the 207th day of the proceedings, I would like to greet everyone present, members of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, and everyone else in and around the courtroom. I spent part of the night thinking about how we should proceed; I know that the registrar did so, too. And I believe that the best way to save time would be to start tomorrow at 9.00 with an ex parte hearing, which would take 10 minutes. Then we'll have a half an hour break, which means that the actual hearing should start at 9.45 tomorrow. The ex parte hearing will then start at 9.00 tomorrow, and at quarter to 10.00 we can start with the actual hearing. This is necessary because the tapes have to be changed. We'll try and shorten the break in order to save time. Without wasting more time, we'll now call the witness into the courtroom. Defence counsel have said that they will need another 45 minutes to complete their examination-in-chief. So I will be giving them the floor in a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. If you can hear the interpretation, you may sit down and the examination-in-chief, so I will be giving them the floor in a minute. Good morning, sir. If you can hear the interpretation, you may sit down, and the examination-in-chief will now continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I can hear you very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Terzic, at the end of the day yesterday we were discussing events in the village of Miletici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Mr. President, for the sake of the transcript, I would first like to say that the document that we showed in our list, number 9 in the bundle, in fact this is not a new document; it's a document tendered by Mr. Hadzihasanovic's Defence, so I apologise to my colleagues. It's not necessary to look at the document again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Terzic, at the beginning of June 1993, where were you?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of June 1993 I went to Travnik to have a rest. I was on regular leave, but on the 6th or 7th the HVO engaged in combat against the army. So as an operations officer I joined the unit and I established contact immediately with the unit and I continued to perform my duties as an operations officer during the conflict itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade was engaged?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion with a company, a small company, of 60 to 70 people who were on leave was then engaged. They were assigned a task by the commander of the Operations Group, by General Alagic. They were engaged in Hajdareve Njive. That was the first task. They had to carry out because in the immediate vicinity of the barracks -- that was in the immediate vicinity of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where is Hajdareve Njive --

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hajdareve Njive is 3 to 400 metres as the crow flies from the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In front of the building where the building of the 1st Battalion was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is that 3 or 400 metres from Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in Travnik, above where the unit was located or rather where the command of the 1st Battalion was located. It's as the crow flies, as I have said. And if you go by road it's further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, since not everything has been entered in the transcript, if I have understood you correctly, it's 3 to 400 metres as the crow flies from the town of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the town of Travnik, but it's on a slope. It is 3 to 400 metres away in front of the building on the hill of Bukovica, halfway up the Bukovica hill. And to the right there is a place called Gradac or small hill called Gradac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Terzic, could you have a look at a document in the bundle of documents, the document is document 16, document number 17, and document number 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, it's document DK19.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at item 2, our forces.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you have a look at item 2, where it says "our forces," if you have found that in the document. Document number 16.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Units of the 17th Glorious Mountain Brigade." Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Further down below.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade is engaged in Hajdareve Njive, linking with itself and covering with" -- I apologise. "The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade is engaged in the direction towards Hajdareve Njive, linking it to itself and covering it with its mortars. Units of the territorial structure are linked in the 17th glorious Mountain Brigade and are independently acting in the village of Bojna."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: It's not necessary to continue. If -- when you're reading could you read more slowly for the sake of the interpretation. Could you have a look at document 17, it's a new document. Is this a report on the activities of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade in Hajdareve Njive?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you have a look at the following document, document number 18. It's document P465. A combat report from the Bosanska Krajina OG. Could you just have a look at the date. It's the 8th of June, 1993. Please just have a look at the last sentence in the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Battalion in the 7th Muslim Brigade is attacking the Hajdareve Njive feature and is engaged in the direction of Bukovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at the beginning of the report where it says "the command of the OG."

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The command of the Bosanska Krajina OG, the 8th of June, 1993, at 1900 hours, regular operations report."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It means that it was drafted at 1900 hours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terzic, yesterday and today we have discussed the events in Miletici and in Maline, or rather the events that occurred at the beginning of June 1993. Did you and the brigade or the battalion ever receive a request for the unit to report its superior command to someone else about the events in Miletici and Maline in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terzic, I have a few questions for you about soldiers, members of the 7th Brigade. Were the soldiers of the 7th Muslim Brigade of the ABiH, did they have documents on them which indicated whether they were army members or not?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the 7th Muslim had to have orders on them regulating the movement of the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade; this was to be in accordance with the corps orders, according to which members of a unit could circulate when on leave and these orders also mentioned how they should carry out their tasks. When on leave they had to have documents on them and authorisation to be on leave. They also had to leave their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at the documents number 6 and 7 in the bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, these documents are new documents, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Documents 5 and 6 are the ones I'm referring to. When you've seen the -- when you've had a look at the documents, tell me whether this is what you were just referring to in response to my question.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the basis of an order from the command of the 3rd Corps; strictly confidential" --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you read through that slowly.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to an order of the command of 3rd Corps; strictly confidential; number 01419/3; dated the 17th of February, 1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Terzic, allow me to interrupt you. Could you just read out item 1.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Order. Each member of our brigade when wearing his uniform has to have appropriate documents with him, military ID, and displaying his evidence of membership in the unit."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please have a look at document number 6, item 1.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Order. All soldiers who are not on duty are forbidden to carry weapons outside the unit, not even in the case of increased tension because if the soldier goes home on leave the unit is obliged to provide him with an escort."

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terzic, do you know Mr. Kubura?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In 1993 do you know what Mr. Kubura was?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff, the Chief of Staff in the brigade. When he arrived there and perhaps at the end of August or the beginning of September he was appointed as brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we only have one more proposal to make. Could this witness and everyone else be shown the following video: P482 is the exhibit number. And after having shown the video, we will have completed our examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I've shown this video to you in the course of the proofing. I only have one question. Could you see whether anyone from the command of the 7th Muslim Brigade or any member of the 7th Muslim Brigade was in the video?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one was in the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This completes our examination-in-chief. I'd just like to ask the witness to sign and date the map he was shown yesterday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, could you put your name and last name on the map that you have next to you. Could you sign it and date it. The date today is the 12th of April, 2005. Right then. I would like to turn to the Prosecution. Do you have any objections to this map being tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can we have the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. So it is Defence document DK28. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I might, for the record, if we could have an indication as to whether the Hadzihasanovic Defence team has any objections to that map being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Since they were not asking for the floor, I thought they had nothing to say. You have the floor, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to stress we have no objections, but silence is not normally recorded in the transcript. So it is very helpful of my colleague to remind us that we should say this out loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we've had a couple of new documents. I don't know whether we should sort it out now or when we are finished with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll see about that later after the cross-examination. I'd like to give the floor to the Prosecution now for the cross-examination of this floor -- unless, of course -- since again you did not say anything. Do you have any questions now?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at this stage. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. My name is Daryl -- my name is Daryl Mundis and along with my colleagues here this morning we represent the Prosecution in this case. I have a few questions for you, sir, but before I start let me assure you that it is not in any way my intention to confuse you. And I would ask you, sir, if you don't understand any of my questions to simply inform me of that and I will rephrase the questions so that you do understand it. Is that clear, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's -- let's go back, sir, and start a little bit at the beginning. You told us that you were part of the Muslim forces in Travnik. Can you tell us, sir, when you first joined that formation.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the first time I joined the ranks on the 10th of May, 1992, when people were registered, and they were registered officially, as a unit in the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I take it then, sir, that you joined the Muslim forces in Travnik at the time that unit was created?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what position, if any, did you hold within that unit and what rank, if any, did you hold in May 1992 when you joined that unit?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that stage there were no ranks in the army. I was a noncommissioned officer in the former JNA, and so I was an officer there. And I had spent at an officers' school for noncommissioned officers at Bileca for six months.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there come a time, sir, when you acquired some type of rank? And I'm again specifically referring to the time when you were with the Muslim forces in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no ranks there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what function or what role, if any, did you play within that unit, the Muslim forces in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The technical role was of operative nature, to organise the structure and the attachments and to somehow make it look like an army unit, to organise the structure of the unit in order to make it functional. Preparations -- the induction of the unit of a purely technical nature in order to indicate who was in what unit, what company, what detachment. So I was a kind of instructor there, somebody who had gone to this officers' school, and as somebody who was familiar with the structure of the military organisation I was asked to help out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I believe you told us yesterday, sir, that that unit ceased to exist once the brigades of the 3rd Corps were formed approximately in mid-November 1992. Is that what you told us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, at any point in time between the 10th of May, 1992, when you joined the Muslim forces and when that unit ceased to exist sometime in mid-November 1992, did you at any point in time during that period obtain or receive any type of rank?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At that stage we did not have any ranks as yet. We had no officers, et cetera. This was a rank that I had been given before, prior to the war, as a reserve officer in the armed forces of the former Yugoslavia as a reserve captain of the foot soldiers -- the ground forces --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, the interpreter made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Infantry. And I had gone to this officer's school at Bileca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I see that you still have the bundle of Defence documents next to you. Could you please turn to the document under tab 2, which for the record is P695. If you could look at tab 2; you were shown this document yesterday. Now, sir, the entry under number 4 on this list on the first page, would that in fact be you, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I see, sir, in the far right column a -- this document lists you as being a captain?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a captain on the basis of the reserve forces of the former Yugoslavia because I had attended the reserve officers' school at Bileca in 1983 when they had courses there. It was between six and seven months, and then we did exercises, et cetera. Once you finish that school, you would be the 2nd Lieutenant. And then after -- at each separate exercise you would be promoted in rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, of the 80 names that are listed on this document you told us yesterday that some of these people, and this is on page 71, some of them entered the 7th Muslim Brigade, whereas the others probably entered the 306th, the 325th, the 17th, and some other brigades that existed at that time in that area. Do you know of the 80 names that are on this list, P695, how many of those people joined the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade after it was established in November 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly, between 60 -- 40 and 60 per cent, 50 per cent, I don't know. I suppose you can look into the documents of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. You can find out exactly, but I think on average 50 to 60 per cent and the rest went to other units when they were being formed. But nobody could go anywhere until they were mobilised, then told to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, which unit or what organisation, what structure, would have mobilised these people and told them which unit to go to?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mobilisation went through the defence secretariat of the municipality of Travnik and other municipal secretariats which was involved in that. And then, for example, if there was a recruiter expressing a wish in that respect, they would -- first of all, their names would be taken and then they would be channeled to relevant units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were shown at the very beginning of your testimony yesterday a videotape from August of 1992. Do you remember watching that videotape?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which, again for the record, is Prosecution Exhibit P762. And you told us that you recognised yourself on that videotape?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you told us, sir, that that was an oath, that the scene depicted on that videotape was an oath. And this is on page 69 and 70. You said: "An oath taken by every unit, a traditional one, ordered and prescribed for every single unit of the BH army. There was the commander of the unit, and then we had religious and political leaders of the municipality of Travnik." Can I ask you, sir, which religious and political leaders were present on that day and are visible in the videotape?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that on that day, and I believe I noticed it yesterday, there was a commander -- the commander of my unit. So I saw Muftija Tradjki [phoen] and then I saw quite a few people from the population and then people who were prominent economic leaders. For example, there was a -- the manager of a clothing factory. They had about 7.000 staff at the time, and I saw some other people. And I think that invitations had been extended to all those who were meant to attend, and I don't know whether because of their own engagements they all had time to attend. As to attendance and all that, I don't really know because at the time there were quite a few units which had already become operational, which were already out in the field, or were involved in preparations because combat activities were underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if I were to show you again that five-minute video clip in its entirety, would you be in a position to identify the people that you've told us you recognised or knew?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave I would again ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 762, that is about a five or five-and-a-half minute shown yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Witness, as we're preparing that video and as the usher perhaps puts your monitor on the right setting, I would ask you that we take a slightly different course of action from was taken by my learned colleagues yesterday; that is, as you watch the videotape when you see persons or a person that you know or recognise, including yourself, if you will simply tell us to stop and we will pause the videotape so that you can describe for us who it is that you're identifying. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me also tell you before we do this, sir, that as the videotape pauses it will get even more grainy and difficult to see than it already is, but we'll try to do the best with what we have. So, sir, if at any point you see someone that you know or recognise, just tell us to stop and we'll pause the videotape, and I'll ask you to describe the person that you've identified.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can stop it now perhaps. This is the commander of the unit in front of all of us. His name is Emir Redzic called Tara. And then to his left, Ahmed Adilovic and PDVP.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, when you say the commander of the unit, Emir Redzic, is he the person holding the megaphone in this video?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahmed Adilovic and PDVP and VP, and there is a person holding the microphone there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know who the person is holding the microphone or the megaphone?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahmed Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, where in this picture or on this video did you see Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left. Or if we look to the left there is Emir Redzic who was the then-commander of the Muslim forces detachment. I think that he would sign his name as a lieutenant colonel, but he was an active member of the armed forces and he had gone to the military academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've also given us in the English transcript two abbreviations. I believe you said PDVP and VP. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what those acronyms stand for?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the information, propaganda, and religious affairs, in charge of information, propaganda, and religious affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that was the position that Mr. Adilovic?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Adilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please continue with the videotape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are two fighters who were members of this unit. I think Ravka Rajko [phoen], and I can't remember the name of the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. We can continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The photographer wearing a yellow T-shirt, Enver Palalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And was he with the media, sir, or what was his function?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander, Emir Redzic is in front of us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The mufti of Travnik is here. You can see him here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what is the mufti of Travnik wearing, what type of clothing?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's wearing this solemn religious robes, either official or solemn or something. I'm not really familiar with that sort of jargon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It would be fair to say that he's the individual in the white robes with the white head covering. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And his name is Mufti Abdibegovic?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, the person holding the megaphone, do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I wasn't interested either.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here again we can see Ahmet Adilovic and Emir Redzic standing behind the Mufti of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And there, too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's Mehmed Corhodzic who at the time was the commander of base 3 logistical -- logistics base 3 for the provisions to the Municipal Staff of Territorial Defence, but he was also the director or the managing director of the clothing factory at Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, sir. Let me ask you a couple of follow-up questions. When we stopped the videotape you told us that you saw the Mufti of Travnik, and I asked you about the person standing next to him holding the megaphone. And you told us that you didn't know who that person was and I'm quoting on page 17, line 9: "I wasn't interested either." Can you tell us why you weren't interested in who this person was?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a professional there, and since I was in a position that I had to carry out a technical task or finish up on a job, I mean what was my concern was for me to be able to complete the task that had been entrusted to me that I was working on at the time. So I was not particularly concerned with all those things. There were probably who were in charge of protocol and of all the events that had taken place during the day, people who were in charge of information, propaganda, and all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was the person that was visible next to the Mufti one of the religious or political leaders of the municipality of Travnik who was attending this function?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person standing next to the mufti, yes. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. It's a bit unclear from the transcript, sir. Let me ask the question again. The person visible in the video next to the mufti, was he one of the religious or political leaders of the municipality of Travnik who was attending this function?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge, sir, as to why this person was invited to attend this function and to address the Muslim forces in Travnik on this day in August 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't responsible for such things, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me move on to a slightly different topic or a different topic. Once the 7th Muslim Brigade was established in November 1992, you told us that you joined that unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what was your function in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade at the time you joined that unit?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I joined the 7th Muslim, I was an officer for operations and training. This is an establishment post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, based on the description that you told us earlier this morning of your role within the Muslim forces in Travnik, would it be fair to say that what you were doing for the Muslim forces in Travnik also involved operations and training?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, preparing something, technically organising something, means dividing tasks, specifying tasks assigned, et cetera. The commander issues tasks, and in the course of a plan for activity that is drafted in the course of a day, a week, or a month, you carry out the tasks planned by the commander and you carry them out on the basis of orders from your superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, did your responsibilities during the time period you were with the Muslim forces in Travnik include operations and training of that unit in order to get them ready for combat?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was a plan issued by the commander and a period for preparation had been specified, a period for training, or if troops were to be trained in the use of weapons then these preparations would be carried out in accordance with the plan issued by the commander. The commander would issue plans that had to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, at any point in time from May 1992 through November 1992 when you were with the Muslim forces in Travnik, were you assisted in any of these -- in carrying out any of these plans or training by foreigners, by members of the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I couldn't answer that question. I wasn't familiar with those tasks. I don't know. There's nothing I could say. We provide -- we obtained regular supplies from the logistics base in the Travnik Municipal Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the time period from the summer of 1992 through November of 1992, did you have any personal communication or involvement with any of the foreign fighters who came into Bosnia who was later known as the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I would come across them in town. Perhaps I had some form of contact with them, quite by chance, but nothing of any substance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, at any point in time while you were with the Muslim forces in Travnik whether any soldiers from the Muslim forces in Travnik received any type of training from these foreign fighters who were later known as the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. That wasn't necessary because most of the men from the -- most of us were from the former army. We completed our military service, and the others, commanders of detachments, platoons, et cetera, would train their own troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you -- have you ever heard at any point in time of the name of one of the foreigners -- foreign fighters who was in Central Bosnia by the name of Abdul Aziz?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Perhaps I heard this name quite by chance, but not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's return now to the time period after November 1992 when the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was established. You told us, sir, that initially your responsibilities were for operations and training within the brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Officer for operations and training, well that means that you have to train units according to the plans of the brigade and the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, at this point in time, sir, in November, mid-November 1992, where was your office, or where did you physically go at this point in time to conduct your military duties?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In November when the 7th Muslim was established by an order issued, I went to Zenica where the command was located. I was given an office where the Brigade Staff was located. And in the staff I assumed the duties of an officer for operations and training.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, how long did you remain in that post holding the duties responsible for operations and training within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained in that post of an officer for operations and training up until the 14th of February, 1994, when I became assistant commander for logistics in the -- in a light --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, for the record, could you please repeat the unit that you joined after the 14th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th of February, 1994, I joined the 37th Light Muslim Liberation Brigade as assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, at any point in time from the middle of November 1992 until the 14th of February, 1994, when you joined the 37th Light Muslim Liberation Brigade, did you serve as the commander of a battalion within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have such duties, but the task of the Chief of Staff, when you are told to go to a zone of responsibility and to carry out tasks that had to be carried out at the time, well, you'd receive a field task. You would have to go to the forward command post and you would have to go to the zone of responsibility of your brigade, the zone of responsibility assigned to you by the corps. We had a zone of responsibility, as I said yesterday, and I used the map to show you the zone that was from Kazici to elevation 1260 and we had that zone of responsibility, the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you're telling us, sir, that at not point in time were you the commander of a battalion within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during this period from mid-November 1992 through 14 February 1994 your duty post remained in the headquarters of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But if the unit wasn't assigned combat tasks then the staff would be moved, the unit would be moved, and then tasks would be carried out later perhaps over a period of 20 days or a month, it depended. In the meantime troops would be on leave, they would go home, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. But I just want to make sure, sir, that I understand what you'll telling us, and that is that throughout the period from mid-November 1992 until the 14th of February, 1994, you were assigned to the staff of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were asked a few questions earlier this morning about the accused, Brigadier Kubura, and you told us sometime in the August or beginning of September 1993 he was assigned responsibilities of commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's an order which states when he was appointed as commander. So I can't be precise. This is not my field. I don't know when he was promoted and appointed as commander. I think there is an order. I think that's the period concerned, but you should refer to the order in which he was appointed as commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, prior to that time period when Brigadier Kubura was assigned or appointed as commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, what position did he hold?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant -- a Chief of Staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade. He was the Chief of Staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at the same time he was also the deputy commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the commander was absent or prevented from performing his duties, he would replace the commander, but he wasn't the commander. When the commander leaves, he would appoint or issue an order stating who would act as commander on his behalf during his absence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the time you joined the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in mid-November 1992, who was the commander of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Asim Koricic. I think it was Asim Koricic at the time, but I think you have orders stating which individuals are being appointed as commanders. A lot of time has passed since then, so I can't remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how long, sir, did Asim Koricic remain the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right up until the point in time when Brigadier Kubura was appointed to that post in an official document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, let me ask you this: When was the last time you personally saw or spoke with Asim Koricic?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean recently or at that time? Well, let's say a year ago if we're talking about the year 2004. We happen to bump into each other, so we had a chat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, about the time period from mid-November 1992 until 14 February 1994 when you left the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. During that time period -- well, let's be more specific. From the time you joined the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in mid-November 1992 until the time Brigadier Kubura was appointed commander of that brigade, how frequently did you see Mr. Koricic?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the time he went abroad. I wouldn't know whether that was January, February, or March, but I know for sure that it wasn't after March or April. He wasn't in the brigade then or I didn't meet him. Since my duties did not have to do with the commander that had to do with the Chief of Staff and the Chiefs of Staffs of other services, I heard that he went abroad. I had heard that he went abroad and that there was only the Chief of Staff, Brigadier Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you're telling us, sir, that sometime in the first few months of 1993, Commander Koricic went abroad. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And from the time period that he went abroad until commander -- until Brigadier Kubura was appointed as the commander, did you have or did you receive any communications or any orders or any assignments from Mr. Koricic?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you, sir, as the person responsible for operations and training within that brigade know where Mr. Koricic was?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know for sure whether it was -- whether he was in Austria, Germany, or Switzerland, but I knew he was abroad. Given all the duties I had to perform, I didn't try to find out much about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, during the time period after the first few months of 1993 when Mr. Koricic went abroad, did he leave you or anyone in the command with a forwarding address or a telephone number where he should be contacted to carry out his duties as commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He didn't leave any contact details for me, and that wasn't necessary because I was far below the rank of a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during this time period, sir, following Mr. Koricic's trip abroad until Mr. Kubura was appointed as the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, who was in charge? Who commanded the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff according to the post he was assigned to, but he had assistant commanders who covered various fields at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say the Chief of Staff you're referring to Brigadier Kubura. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm referring to Brigadier Kubura.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And just so that we're clear then, sir, once Mr. Koricic went abroad sometime between January and April 1993 until his formal appointment in August or September 1993, Amir Kubura commanded the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the duties he had as Chief of Staff, he replaced the commander. He assigned tasks and issued instructions together with his assistant commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you now, sir, a couple of questions concerning Ramo Durmis. The Defence asked you some questions about Ramo Durmis and you told us that -- let me start a different way. You told us that at some point in time that Mr. Durmis left the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, to the best of your recollection, when did Ramo Durmis leave the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramo Durmis left perhaps at the beginning of January 1993 after the action in Visegrad [as interpreted] on the 28th of December, 1992. When this action came to an end, we had a number of dead and wounded men. And at the beginning of January, Ramo Durmis and some of his soldiers left the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, it says in the English transcript at page 27, line 2 "it was after the action in Visegrad." I believe that was actually Visoko. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Visoko, Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, what is the basis, sir, for you telling us that Mr. Durmis and some of his soldiers left the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade at the beginning of January 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I had a look at a number of documents and reference was made to him leaving the unit in January. This was a revolt. He showed his characteristic stubbornness. He left the 7th Muslim Brigade and took those young men with him, and he didn't return to the 7th Muslim because at the time he was the commander of the 1st Company. He accused others of significant losses in Visegrad and Visoko, and there was a revolt that he couldn't control and that is why he left the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, you told us that: "He showed his characteristic stubbornness." Did you know Ramo Durmis prior to the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that in the middle of April 1993 the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and its commander, Ramo Durmis, were specifically cited by the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, they were awarded?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that proposal, a result of the battle at the battlefield in Visoko -- rather the Visegrad elevation. I heard that a proposal had been made for his efforts, but I don't know when he was given this award.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask, Mr. President, with the assistance of the usher and the registrar that the witness with shown Prosecution Exhibit P727. Perhaps if that document could be put on the ELMO. Unfortunately due to time constraints, Mr. President, we weren't able to make sufficient copies, but I would ask that it be put onto the ELMO so everybody can take a look at it. I would specifically ask -- well, first of all, if the witness can take a look at the document so he can see what it is we're asking him to look at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Given the efforts and results obtained in battle on Allah's way and the unselfish dedication shown when carrying out combat operations, and given the fact that his patriotic duties have been performed in our Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in order to commemorate the anniversary of the day of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I hereby order that the following stimulative measures be taken. An award in the form of money is to be granted to the following members of the 7th Muslim Brigade: Serif Patkovic, Azar Bektas, Ramiz Savic, Nusret Ibricic, Suad Jusovic" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you to go on this document to section 4 on that page. And if we look under Roman numeral IV, small letter "b," and under that the first bullet point. Do you see the reference there to the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion and its commander Ramo Durmis?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you see that this document was in fact signed? Perhaps if the --

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the document is actually signed by Brigadier Kubura, is it not?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me turn, sir, in the final few moments that I have remaining to another document that's in the bundle of documents that the Defence provided you with. I would ask you, sir, if you could turn in that bundle of documents to tab 14. There are a number of documents or a number of pages behind tab 14, and I'm specifically interested in the second page of this document, which for the record I believe is P474. Was this a document, sir, that was drafted by yourself or prepared for your approval by a member of your staff?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to go back to the first document. This is a document that I drafted; it's my operations report to the brigade and the Bosnian Krajina OG. It's been signed and I stand by this document. I don't stand by the other document because there is no signature. I can see that the address of the person it was forwarded to is not -- has not been written down and it's not the typical type of military document you usually see. This document has a date, 336/93, and has a protocol number, the name of the unit and number. I can stand by the first document, the one that precedes this one. But the second document is not a document that I drafted. I didn't sign it. It's not my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me ask you this then, sir: Were you aware at any point in time in the first six months of 1993 whether there were any units of the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in the area of Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will now ask Defence counsel whether they have any re-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We only have a few additional questions. I don't know whether this is the appropriate time or whether we should commence after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead -- or in fact you would prefer to continue after the break. In that case, it is 10.25. We'll now have our break and we will resume at about 10 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Defence has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have just a couple of questions and I would like for the document that my colleague has shown to the witness, P727, to be shown again -- to be shown to the witness again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Terzic, before the break when you were answering the questions by my colleague you said that the proposal for an award when he mentioned the name of Ramo Durmis you said that it was in connection with what was taking place in the course of the battle for Visegrad and Visoko. That battle was at what time?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 28th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Was that proposal for an award and that award referred to something that happened in the past or in 1993 or at that time?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The praise and the awards were referred to the battle which took place on the 28th of December and the results were outstanding, and it was a huge success for the entire unit, I mean these are the commanders of the unit that was engaged there in the area of Visegrad, the place called Visoko in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like you to look at document 1 in items 1, 2, and 3. You have references to awards and praises for individuals?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In item 4 it says: "I praise the following units ..." Does point 4 refer to individuals or units within the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 4: "I praise the following units from the Battalion, the 7th Muslim Battalion the rank of Battalion." In point B the rank of company, the 1st Company of the 1st Battalion, and the company commander is Durmis Ramo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could I ask you something else and my colleague has asked you the same question as well. When Mr. Kubura was acting as commander in the period of time we have been referring to, did you address him as Chief of Staff or commander?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And another question. Do you know the exact date when Mr. Koricic left the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the other Defence lawyers?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we've already had cross-examination and we have no questions now. If we do, it will be after the Judges' questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned I have some clarification points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like you to confirm clearly that when you were at the 7th Brigade your job was to deal with the structure and the formation within the Chief of Staff. Was that your official job within the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you take a look at the document number 17 in this binder. It is dated the 6th of June, 1993. It is a combat report in fact. Could you tell me who signed this document.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This doesn't look like my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not your signature?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did draft the report, but it may well happen that somebody else has signed it because I was not allowed to sign as a battalion commander because I was not even an acting battalion commander or a commander of a unit in the 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're saying that you did have a draft combat report. It was not you who typed it up?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, is it the person who actually typed it up that should be signed as battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, believe me. It was up to me to give a summary of events during the day, to draw up a report for our superiors so they would be informed about what we had been doing on any given day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 6th of June -- well, who was the battalion commander on that day?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that time you will have to look up -- look it up in the personal records. I think Zubaca Ahmed or somebody else. You will have to check it out in the documents belonging to the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. Since we're dealing with the documents now, could you look at document number 2. In document number 2 in the B/C/S version, not the English version but the B/C/S version, next to your name there is a reference indicating your date of birth, the rank of captain, and a number, 31102. What does it correspond to, that number?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military experts will be able to tell you that this is an infantry reference, the type of -- the type of training the got at the reserve officers' school at Bileca in the former Yugoslavia. The -- an infantry captain, so I think this signifies infantry, but military experts can shed more light on it. But this is a number for the military files.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document that you have in front of you on page 1 it says the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the armed forces and the Muslim forces of Travnik. As far as you're concerned, is this a military document?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is entirely in the form of a military document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Within the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992 and 1993 - but here we're talking about 15th of September 1992 - well, what was the official language of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina? What was the official language?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosniak/Croatian/Serbian in the same way. At that time I believe that is what it was, or Serbo-Croat. It is a matter of an official definition. You would have to determine it in some other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what about the Arab language? Was it used at all within the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you take a look. On page 4 there is a stamp on page 4 -- 3, sorry. You'll see that there is a stamp. There is a saber there and there is some kind of writing in the B/C/S language. And on top of that how do you explain the rest of the seal?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this is at the very start when the armed forces and the army units were being set up at that time, local units or, for example, Bosnian Dragons or Gradina detachment, or some other names. I mean, this had not been standardised yet. There was not a protocol. The armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina were only being set up. It is a failure on the part of the commander who would have had to instruct the units on how to communicate and how to introduce markings and references for their units. I believe this was done later, but that was the whole point creating those brigades in order to have a uniform approach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to move on to another topic. Earlier on when answering the questions you have explained that in the beginning of June 1993 you were on holiday and then when you found out about the HVO offensive you reported straight away to the 7th Brigade. And whilst listening to your reply, I notice that you even added that the battalion was resting. Now, my question is this: War had been declared and even so there were holiday periods when nobody was there. How did it work?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I didn't express myself clearly. They were not rested. They were not resting. They had people engaged in three areas. First of all in Vitez in the village of Batalica, then Ravno Rostovo, you see, and third unit which was in the area of responsibility of the 7th Muslim Brigade, and a part of the unit where soldiers were allowed to take leave. In the beginning of June or slightly earlier with the approval of the -- of our superiors there was a change there and so for the people who had not had any leave for 60 days. So we left the answer to the unit in their area of responsibility. And from the 17th Krajiska unit we got 60 unarmed soldiers who took those weapons and were using in their territory. So the people who were on leave could have some time off, but most of those people were still in the barracks because they had no other homes and they were still available. And when combat operations started, they were given the first combat task, that is to say to attack Hajdareve Njive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you yourself, your office was located where exactly when you were within the 7th Brigade? Where was your office?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My office when I was at the Command Staff was at Zenica unless on the basis of orders from the Chief of Staff, somebody else, I was asked to go to the area of responsibility, Kazici 1260, or the barracks in Travnik in case I was asked to do whatever there was to do with regard to the Travnik Battalion as operations expert, to check whether the technical approach within the unit was right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Earlier on on this video you saw yourself on the tape. So initially you were in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Afterwards you were within the 7 Brigade. Now, on the day that you left Travnik --

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was once the 7th Brigade was set up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. So on the day you left Travnik to go to Zenica where you had an office, who did you meet? Who did you meet the first time that you went to Zenica? Who was the highest ranking officer welcoming you to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the occasion of the setting up of the unit when the command issued the orders with regard to the setting up of the 7th Brigade, then the commander, the Chief of Staff, and the commander's assistants did all that. And so when I received the orders, or rather the task to go and report to them in Zenica, I had to report to the commander, or rather the Chief of Staff of the brigade to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. You reported to the Chief of Staff, who was it?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in November or December when I got there. At the time it was Asim Koricic who received me and he gave me the task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good. Now, Asim Koricic, did he have an office.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And where was his office? What building? What floor? Could you specify that a bit better as to Koricic's office?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the second floor in the Bilmiste building, the Bilmiste school building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Bilmiste then. So you first saw Koricic and then who did you see? Who did you see afterwards?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that I met with his assistants and I talked to them and we talked about the technical part of the job. We started with the preparations for the creation and the setting up after the brigade in line with the relevant provisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. And at that stage you met with General Kubura?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not then. I met him afterwards, by the end of December or the beginning of January, I can't tell you. It's all in the documents; it's all recorded. Since things were happening very fast that there were combat activities, preparations, and various responsibilities, and all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Now, Koricic, how many times did you see him before he disappeared?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to needs. When my task or my line of duty required it or perhaps sometimes in the evening I ran into him. I can't tell you with any degree of precision. Perhaps 15 to 20 times, according to the requirements of my job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And as far as you can remember, the last time you met Koricic was at what time? December? January? February? March? April? What? Could you specify that. Obviously all this was a long time ago, but you can't specify anything at all?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't really be very specific about that, January, March, April. You see, my job was not closely connected to what the commander was doing. I wasn't getting my tasks assigned directly from the commander. I was doing something else. I was not in a position where I could communicate with him a great deal. January, February, March, I'm not at all sure. I can't specify exactly when it was that he left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you told us that according to your knowledge General Kubura was appointed commander of the brigade in the month of August. When General Kubura was in fact appointed as commander of the 7th Brigade, did Koricic come back or have you never seen him again between his departure and the month of August?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not come back by August, but as to whether he showed up again in October or November, I'm not sure, because there was a total blockade and there was a full-blown conflict with the HVO and so I had not seen him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as far as you can remember because you were in the area, Koricic's office was occupied by somebody else or was it left as it was without anyone else using it as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I wasn't paying attention to that. I don't know. But I do know -- I was in touch with Mr. Kubura up until September, August, September. And when the new Chief of Staff was appointed I was talking to him and so on. The regular work within the army, but combat operations were already underway so I wasn't paying any special attention to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. And now this is my last question and it is about this video. You told us in reply to one of the questions that this event for the Military Staff that was present there was within the framework of an oath taking. Whether --

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, when it comes to the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, is there -- is this oath-taking ceremony mandatory?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in the former JNA it was the same?

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what does it consist of, the oath-taking? Could you describe it very briefly, the ceremony I mean.

utterances.speaker: SEMIR TERZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was a standard text for the oath, it gets read out, and the commander reads it out, and the soldiers repeat it after him and that's it I think. I think there is a text from 1992. We should look for it in the archives; I think they have the complete text of the oath, but that is what it's about. There is a standard text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Right then. Judges have no more questions, so I would like to give the floor to the Prosecution once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution has no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No questions either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. Your testimony has just been completed. I'd like to thank you for coming here and answering to our questions on behalf of the Trial Chamber, for answering to both the questions on the part of the Defence and the Prosecution as well as the Judges. I wish you all the best and a pleasant trip home, and I'm going to ask the usher to accompany you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome and thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As to documents, I'd like to give the floor to the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. We propose to tender into evidence the documents we've got here, number 4, order dated the 19th of February, 1993; then number 5, the order dated the 19th of February, 1993; the document number 6, the order dated the 19th of February, 1993; document number 7, weekly report 261/93, dated the 23rd of February, 1993; number 8, report number 378/93, dated the 14th of March, 1993; number 17, combat report number 357/193, dated the 6th of June, 1993; and number 20, order number 735/93, dated 17th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly it was 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 17, and 20?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm just wondering if perhaps with respect to document number 8 and document number 20 if our learned colleagues can give us an indication as to the source of those documents. I note that the other documents that they have tendered all contain ERN numbers and consequently I can quickly trace where those came from and in fact were disclosed to the Defence by the Prosecution. But I don't seem to see any such numbers on documents 8 and 20, and I wonder if we could get an indication as to where those documents were located or the source of those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right, on 8 and 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have forgotten to mention the fact that these are the new documents and they come from the archives from the armed forces of the Bosnia and Herzegovina in the 7th Brigade, and we had some earlier documents in much the same way as Mr. Hadzihasanovic's Defence team. So we did some research in the archives of Bosnia and Herzegovina as well as the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right then. So the archives of the 7th Brigade. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution has no objection to these documents being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No comment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. So we've got a series of seven documents tendered by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give you the references in English. [In English] The first document dated the 19th of February, 1993, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK 29 with an English version DK29/E. The second document dated the same date with internal reference number 241/93 is admitted into evidence under the reference DK30 with an English translation DK30/E. The document dated the same date with the internal reference number PM-80/93 is admitted into evidence under the reference DK31 with an English translation DK31/E. The document dated 23rd of February, 1993, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK32, with an English translation DK32/E. The document dated 14th of March, 1993, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK33, with an English translation DK33/E. The document dated 6th of June, 1993, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK34, with an English translation DK34/E. And the last document dated 17th of August, 1993, is admitted into evidence under the reference DK35, with an English translation DK35/E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. I'm going to ask the usher to bring in the witness. The Defence is planning on an hour and a half I believe. Can you confirm that, the duration?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that the examination-in-chief will last three-quarters of an hour at the most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good day, sir. I would first like to make sure that the equipment is functioning properly. Are you receiving the interpretation of what I'm saying? If so, please say yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you have been called here as a witness for Brigadier Kubura's Defence. Before you take the solemn declaration could you please tell me your first and last name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Enver Adilovic. I was born on the 10th of January, 1960.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the village of Kljaci in the municipality of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you currently employed or have you retired? What do you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm currently unemployed. I was in the federation army up until 2001, but I'm not employed at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992 and 1993 did you hold a position of any kind? Were you a member of the military and, if so, which unit were you a member of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1992 I was a member of the Vitez detachment, the Novi Grad detachment of the Vitez Territorial Defence Staff. That was right up until the time when the 7th Muslim Brigade was established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When were you assigned to the 7th Muslim Brigade? Do you remember the precise date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was immediately on the 16th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you have a specific post and a rank in the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later I had the establishment post of a company commander. I think that was towards the end of February. And at the time -- I'm not sure about the ranks but I had the establishment rank of a company commander. So I left the war, or rather the federation army with the rank of captain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you already testified before an international or national court with regard to the events that took place in your country in 1992 and 1993, or is this the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time. I've never testified before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read out the text of the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.
